svg.title: How the MUbind package fits together
svg.desc: The CLI starts setup, training, sampling, binder design, benchmark evaluation, persistent model providers and the result viewer. Preprocessing downloads and filters ProstT5 proteins and writes prepared arrays. Dataset loads and embeds those arrays into batches, and also decodes generated vectors. Training selects tasks and masks, computes a noisy prediction and loss, updates the U-Net weights and their exponential moving average, and saves checkpoints. Inference uses a trained or downloaded checkpoint, optional property, structural and seed conditions, and optional target/scaffold input to sample sequences or design binders. Training and inference both use model, the conditioned U-Net denoiser, and diffusion, the shared noise schedule, training objective and loss, and DDPM or DDIM reverse sampler. Inference uses dataset decoding to turn sampled vectors into sequences, and binder design includes scaffold preparation, folding and ranking. Evaluation validates training progress using denoising and sequence or structure metrics. Benchmarks compare saved checkpoints by reusing inference sampling and evaluation utilities. Setup installs MUbind and external model weights, tools and runtimes, including Complexa, ESMFold2, ESMC and Foldseek. Common holds sequence property calculations and shared progress and sequence utilities. The picture shows the main workflow and reuse relationships, not every Python import.
